findings.title: Substring match treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring test `"event.type:error" in query`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) or `event.type:error_foo` also contains that substring, so the function returns True. For the `discover` dataset this causes `count()` to be rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (i.e. `sum(sample_weight)`) for a query that explicitly excludes error events, producing wrong numbers for transaction/other rows (or a Snuba error because `sample_weight` is not populated for non-error rows). The check needs to parse the search query (or at least exclude negations) rather than a naive substring test.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility computed from outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first argument but passes the closure-level `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`) `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (`discover`, `split_dataset`, etc.) while the outer `dataset` is still the metrics/transactions dataset. As a result the dataset-based gate (`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) is evaluated against the wrong dataset: upsampling can be skipped for error queries actually run against `discover`, or applied to a run that was switched to a transaction-like dataset. The check must use `scoped_dataset`.

findings.title: Caching a global option behind a per-org/per-project key yields stale, inconsistent results
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the result of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` for 60s under a key built from `organization.id` plus a hash of the project id set. The underlying data is the *global* option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, which Sentry's options layer already caches in-process; writing/reading a remote cache entry per org+project-set combination adds a cache round trip per query (and the split-dataset path calls this up to 4 times per request) while providing no real speedup. Worse, when the allowlist is changed, queries keep returning the previous decision for up to 60 seconds, so the same chart can flip between upsampled (x10) and raw counts between adjacent requests - a visible data-correctness problem for a counting API. Either drop the cache or key it on the option value/version.

findings.title: `hash()` of project ids in the cache key can collide and return another project set's decision
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. `hash` is a 64-bit (32-bit on some builds) value with no collision guarantees, so two different project-id sets inside the same organization can map to the same key. When that happens a non-allowlisted project set will reuse the cached `True` of an allowlisted set (or vice versa), silently multiplying counts by the sample weight for projects that are not configured for upsampling. Use the actual sorted ids (or a cryptographic digest) in the key instead of `hash()`.

findings.title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is dead code and cannot actually invalidate the cache
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the PR, although its docstring states it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency". It also cannot fulfil that promise: the cache key depends on an arbitrary project-id subset, so invalidating after an allowlist change would require enumerating every org/project-id combination that was ever queried. This leaves the misleading impression that stale cache entries are handled, when in practice they are not.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` is exposed as a public discover function with no project gating
findings.body: The new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True` (unlike the neighbouring internal functions), so any API consumer can now request `upsampled_count()` as a field/yAxis on arbitrary discover queries. The aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which is only meaningful for error rows in allowlisted projects; for transactions or non-upsampled errors it will either error out on the missing/unset `sample_weight` column or return meaningless values, bypassing the allowlist checks in `error_upsampling.py` entirely. Mark it private so only the internal transformation can use it.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` declares result type `number` although it returns an integer
findings.body: The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64`, and the function replaces `count()` (declared `default_result_type="integer"` elsewhere in this file), but it declares `default_result_type="number"`. The response `meta` will advertise a different field type than `count()` does, which changes client-side formatting/axis handling for the very charts this feature rewrites.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` only registered for the discover dataset while the errors dataset path returns True
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` unconditionally returns True for `dataset == errors`, so `count()` will be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` for errors-dataset queries. However the function is only added to `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter` in this file; the errors dataset uses its own dataset config/function converter. Unless `upsampled_count` is resolvable there, every errors-dataset timeseries query from an allowlisted project will fail with an "unknown function" validation error. No test in this PR exercises `dataset=errors`, so this path is unverified.

findings.title: No test covers the new caching entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`
findings.body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and the column transform. The public function added by this PR - including the cache key construction, cache hit/miss behaviour, and the interaction between a cached `False`/`True` and the dataset gate - is completely untested, which is exactly where the risky logic (stale cache, hash-based key) lives. Tests should at minimum cover a cache hit returning the stale decision and the empty-project-ids case.

findings.title: Test comments contradict the asserted values
findings.body: `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10  # First bucket has 1 event` (and the following line) claim the bucket contains 1 event while asserting 10. The 10 comes from the 0.1 client sample rate being upsampled; the comments should state that, otherwise a future reader will assume the assertion is wrong and "fix" it.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is an accidentally committed nested checkout of the repository itself; `git submodule update --init` will fail for anyone cloning, and tooling that walks the tree (mypy `files = ["."]`, pytest collection) can behave unpredictably. It should be removed from the commit.

findings.title: Blanket `except Exception: pass` hides malformed error_sampling fixtures
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the `float()` conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. If a test supplies a malformed `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or `contexts` not being a mapping), `sample_rate` is silently not set and the test will then assert on non-upsampled counts, masking the real problem instead of failing loudly. Since this only runs in test fixtures, the errors should propagate (or at least be narrowed to `TypeError/ValueError` with an assertion).
